findings.title: Selected rescue beside non-deflection
findings.claim: At the limit of lost hope, divine help reaches a chosen subset while force toward the culpable group is stated as not deflectable; wider parallels repeat both selected rescue and the no-deflection outcome.
findings.mechanism: The focus places نَصْرُنَا and نُجِّيَ beside لَا يُرَدُّ بَأْسُنَا عَنِ الْقَوْمِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ. The ج ر م earning/result facet lets the culpable group's act meet the consequence directed toward it. In 21:9, rescue of those willed stands beside destruction of the excessive; 6:147 repeats the no-deflection clause after wide mercy and a condition of denial. These contacts join the two outcomes at the focus limit rather than leaving rescue and punishment as unrelated endings.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the hinge as two directions of outcome at once: some are extracted, while the named culpable group has no deflection path.
findings.containment: This does not give a calculable reason for selection or claim that force can never be averted in any setting. 10:98 supplies a different case in which belief before force is fully realized is followed by removal of worldly chastisement. The despair contexts also remain distinct rather than becoming one general rule.

epistemic.reason: A trusted cross-run finding anchors the paired outcome in focus words; exact wider Arabic and registered focus branches support the mechanism. Legacy reader summaries and target passages without target morphology qualify the synthesis.

findings.title: Perceived closure before aid
findings.claim: The focus holds lost hope and a belief of having been denied at the same crisis limit; 6:34 repeats denial and harm before messenger aid, while 10:22 repeats a pressured belief that travelers are enclosed before their plea for rescue.
findings.mechanism: ٱسْتَيْـَٔسَ carries loss of hope; ظَنُّوا frames the following proposition as a belief, and كُذِبُوا keeps the falsity attribution passive. In 6:34, messengers are denied, endure, and are harmed before aid arrives. In 10:22, travelers think they are surrounded by waves before calling to be saved. These separate triggers make the focus's threshold a recurring human crisis without turning perception into a verdict that aid is absent.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can keep the fear and falsity attribution open without mistaking either perception for knowledge that help has ceased.
findings.containment: Neither parallel resolves the exact subject or object of كُذِبُوا in 12:110. The 6:34 recurrence does not decide whether the Yusuf restoration sequence is a general mechanism or an analogy, and the 10:22 comparison is one different crisis rather than a universal law of aid timing.

epistemic.reason: The focus carriers are mapped in the packet and both wider passages supply exact Arabic, but the reader-walk and HFT summaries are legacy_unbound and target morphology is not supplied.

findings.title: A waterway image for arriving relief
findings.claim: As an explicitly analogical image, the help that reaches the messengers can be pictured as a watercourse from a source to a receiving place, while the rescue of some can be pictured as reaching ground beyond the water's reach.
findings.mechanism: The focus's نَصْرُنَا has a mapped watercourse branch whose facet moves from a distant source to a water-collecting place; the adjacent passive rescue names recipients separated from danger. The independent 10:22 scene places travelers in a ship with storm wind and waves arriving from every side, then gives a plea for deliverance. These contacts let the focus's arrival and rescue acts carry a bounded water-and-refuge image.
findings.reader_payoff: The abstract arrival of help becomes imaginable as a channel reaching threatened recipients and lifting some to safety, while the narrated messenger rescue remains intact.
findings.containment: Neither a river, a receiving basin, nor high ground is literally named in 12:110 or 10:22. The watercourse and flood-safe refuge are analogical branch readings, not a claim that the focus narrates a watershed. The supplied 10:22 scene has a ship, wind, waves, and a plea, not a pushing pole; pole-driven propulsion is excluded.
